x: All three are correct: Dharmapala (c. 770-810) installed the puppet Chakrayudha at Kannauj, was defeated by Dhruva and by Nagabhata II near Monghyr, and founded Vikramashila. Hence D.
The order is Gopala (elected founder, mid-8th c.), Devapala, Mahipala I (c. 977-1027) and Ramapala (c. 1072-1126), the last strong Pala ruler. Hence B, D, C, A.
All four are correct: Nagabhata II ousted Chakrayudha, beat Dharmapala near Monghyr, was himself defeated by Rashtrakuta Govinda III, and made Kannauj the Pratihara capital. Hence D.
Bhartribhata I was not a Gurjara-Pratihara ruler (RPSC 2018 key). Nagabhata II, Mahendrapala I and Mahipala I were all Pratihara kings.

All three are correct: Dhruva acted through Vemulavada Arikesari I to beat Vishnuvardhana IV, who then gave his daughter Shila Mahadevi to Dhruva; Amoghavarsha I won at Vingavalli and took the title Viranarayana. Hence D.
Trivikrama (Trivikrama Bhatta) composed Nalachampu, the first Champu. Pampa wrote Vikramarjuna Vijaya, Ponna wrote Santipurana and Viracharya wrote Ganitasaram.

C is wrong: Nandivarman II was the Pallava ruler whose Kanchi Vikramaditya II took three times and spared; he did not overthrow the Rashtrakutas. It was the Rashtrakutas (under Dantidurga) who replaced the Chalukyas. The other three pairs are correct.
